title: Ordering Food
grammarNote: This lesson covers polite request formulas — quisiera, me gustaría, and ¿me trae...? — used as fixed lexical chunks when ordering. It also introduces the indirect object pronouns me/le/nos and the prepositional phrases para mí/para él, all common when ordering food and asking for the check in Mexico.

phrases.target: Quisiera una agua fresca de horchata
phrases.native: I would like a horchata agua fresca
phrases.phonetic: kee-see-EH-rah OO-nah AH-gwah FRES-kah deh or-CHAH-tah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Quisiera' is the polite conditional form of querer, used to soften a request — much more courteous than 'quiero' when ordering food or drinks.

exampleSentence.target: Quisiera una agua fresca de horchata, por favor.
exampleSentence.native: I would like a horchata agua fresca, please.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Quisiera' comes from the imperfect subjunctive of querer but functions as a fixed polite formula meaning 'I would like'; it doesn't change to sound more or less polite, it just softens the request itself.
phrases.memoryHook: Quisiera sounds like 'key-see-AIR-ah' — turn the key gently, quietly asking rather than demanding.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I would like a horchata agua fresca
practiceItems.answer: Quisiera una agua fresca de horchata

practiceItems.prompt: ___ una agua fresca de horchata, por favor.
Estás en la taquería y quieres pedir una bebida de manera cortés. ¿Qué dices?
practiceItems.answer: Quisiera una agua fresca de horchata

phrases.target: Me gustaría probar los tacos al pastor
phrases.native: I would like to try the al pastor tacos
phrases.phonetic: meh goos-tah-REE-ah proh-BAR los TAH-kos al pas-TOR
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Me gustaría' + infinitive is another polite way to express a wish, literally 'it would please me to...'; 'al pastor' describes marinated pork tacos cooked on a vertical spit.

exampleSentence.target: Me gustaría probar los tacos al pastor con salsa verde.
exampleSentence.native: I would like to try the al pastor tacos with green salsa.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Gustaría' agrees with the thing liked, not the person; 'me' marks who is doing the liking — this is the same structure as 'me gusta', just in the conditional.
phrases.memoryHook: Gustaría sounds like 'gusto' (pleasure) + 'ría' (would) — 'it would be my pleasure'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I would like to try the al pastor tacos
practiceItems.answer: Me gustaría probar los tacos al pastor

practiceItems.prompt: Me ___ probar los tacos al pastor.
Nunca has probado los tacos al pastor y quieres pedirlos cortésmente. ¿Qué dices?
practiceItems.answer: Me gustaría probar los tacos al pastor

phrases.target: ¿Me trae una salsa verde, por favor?
phrases.native: Could you bring me a green salsa, please?
phrases.phonetic: meh TRAH-eh OO-nah SAHL-sah VER-deh, por fah-VOR
phrases.vocabularyIntro: '¿Me trae...?' uses the present tense of traer (to bring) with the indirect object pronoun 'me' as a quick, polite way to request an item at the table.

exampleSentence.target: ¿Me trae una salsa verde y unas tortillas, por favor?
exampleSentence.native: Could you bring me a green salsa and some tortillas, please?

phrases.grammarNote: The indirect object pronoun 'me' always goes before the conjugated verb 'trae'; questions like this stay in the present tense rather than the imperative, to sound extra polite.
phrases.memoryHook: Me trae = 'bring ME' — picture the waiter delivering the salsa straight to you.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Could you bring me a green salsa, please?
practiceItems.answer: ¿Me trae una salsa verde, por favor?

practiceItems.prompt: ¿___ trae una salsa verde, por favor?
Quieres que el mesero te traiga salsa verde a la mesa. ¿Qué le preguntas?
practiceItems.answer: ¿Me trae una salsa verde, por favor?

phrases.target: Esto es para mí y esto es para él
phrases.native: This is for me and this is for him
phrases.phonetic: ES-toh es PAH-rah mee ee ES-toh es PAH-rah el
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Para mí' and 'para él' use the preposition 'para' with a prepositional pronoun to clarify who ordered which dish when the waiter serves the table.

exampleSentence.target: El taco de pastor es para mí y la quesadilla es para él.
exampleSentence.native: The al pastor taco is for me and the quesadilla is for him.

phrases.grammarNote: After 'para', personal pronouns switch to their prepositional forms: 'mí' (not 'yo') takes a written accent to distinguish it from the possessive 'mi', while 'él' stays the same as the subject pronoun.
phrases.memoryHook: Mí with an accent points AT me — the little accent mark is like an arrow pointing to yourself.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: This is for me and this is for him
practiceItems.answer: Esto es para mí y esto es para él

practiceItems.prompt: Esto es para ___ y esto es para él.
El mesero no sabe de quién es cada plato en la mesa. ¿Cómo le explicas?
practiceItems.answer: Esto es para mí y esto es para él

phrases.target: ¿Nos puede traer la cuenta, por favor?
phrases.native: Could you bring us the check, please?
phrases.phonetic: nos PWEH-deh trah-ER lah KWEN-tah, por fah-VOR
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Nos' is the indirect object pronoun for 'us', paired with 'poder' + 'traer' to politely ask the waiter to bring something to the whole table.

exampleSentence.target: Ya terminamos. ¿Nos puede traer la cuenta, por favor?
exampleSentence.native: We're finished. Could you bring us the check, please?

phrases.grammarNote: 'Nos' replaces 'a nosotros' and attaches before the conjugated verb 'puede', just like 'me' does for a single person — the object pronoun always precedes the verb in this construction.
phrases.memoryHook: Nos = 'us' — think of 'nosotros' shortened, asking the waiter to bring it TO US.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Could you bring us the check, please?
practiceItems.answer: ¿Nos puede traer la cuenta, por favor?

practiceItems.prompt: ¿___ puede traer la cuenta, por favor?
Tú y tus amigos terminaron de comer y quieren pagar. ¿Qué le dicen al mesero?
practiceItems.answer: ¿Nos puede traer la cuenta, por favor?

phrases.native: Do you have an option without spice?

phrases.target: ¿Le puedo pedir un jugo de naranja?
phrases.native: May I ask you for an orange juice?
phrases.phonetic: leh PWEH-doh peh-DEER oon HOO-goh deh nah-RAN-hah

dialogue.scenario: A waiter takes your drink and food order at a taquería, and you flag a food allergy before asking for the check.
